neighbours.label: ' used' (or a copula before 'accustomed') in the sense of being accustomed to something (are used to, wasn't used to, get used to), not 'used to' for purpose or past habit
fire: If you're used to city life, the quiet here may surprise you.
He never got used to the long winters up north.
The new staff are not used to working such late hours.
Rooms are smaller than you may be used to back home.
Our dog isn't used to being left alone all day.
It takes time to become used to the taste of olives.
Most of the students were used to much easier exams.
Prices are higher than you are accustomed to at home.
quiet: If you have used this tool, the handle here may surprise you.
He used to spend the long winters up north.
The new staff are used by the firm to answer late calls.
Rooms are often used for meetings back at home.
Our dog used to sleep outside all day.
It takes time to explain how olives are used in cooking.
Most of the students used a much easier textbook.
Prices are used to compare the shops at home.

notes: Card: ' used' x24 of the top 32, all 'accustomed' uses; ' adjust', ' adapted', and the top peak on ' are' before accustomed. Probes: 'wasn't used to' 0.564, 'are accustomed to' 0.562 on ' are', 'are used to' 0.518, 'get used to' 0.449; 'is used to drive' 0.004 and 'He used to live' 0.014. A clean distinction: near misses keep the word in its other two senses.
